findings.text: The regex pattern `[0-9;]+m` requires at least one digit or semicolon before `m`, so the valid ANSI reset sequence `\033[m` (no parameters) is not matched and remains as a raw ESC character in XML output, causing XML parsing failures.

The regex only matches ANSI sequences ending with `m`, so other valid control sequences like `\033[2J` (clear screen) or `\033[H` (cursor home) are not removed or escaped, leaving raw ESC characters that corrupt the XML output.

The original code escaped all ESC characters to `` ensuring valid XML; the new code only removes specific color codes, so any non-matching ESC sequences remain unescaped as raw bytes, breaking XML validity for inputs containing cursor movement or other control codes.
